extracted.intended_audience: individual authors (academic and non-academic) applying to the NEH Public Scholars grant program to write nonfiction books in the humanities
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application to the National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholars program to fund the research and writing of a well-researched nonfiction book in the humanities intended for a broad public audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target work: well-researched nonfiction books for the broad public
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program offers grants to individual authors for research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to the creation and publication of well-researched nonfiction books in the humanities written for the broad public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should be aimed at a broad public readership in the humanities; sample funded projects (e.g., film history, British literature, American Civil War, biographies, cultural history) illustrate acceptable topics and scope. The expected output is explicitly a book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: open to individuals; no advanced degree required
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers with or without an academic affiliation may apply, and no advanced degree is required. NEH especially encourages applications from independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both non-academic and academic applicants are welcome; the program continues to offer special encouragement to applicants who have no long-term academic affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum award amount
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use award funds for the permitted activities (research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to the creation and publication of the book). Budgeting should respect this monthly cap and the stated period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance / project duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of performance: Six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project start dates listed (September 1, 2024 and September 1, 2025) indicate expected scheduling; applicants should propose work that fits within a 6–12 month timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected output
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must propose a project that will culminate in a nonfiction book for a broad public audience; sample application narratives provide models of appropriate book-length projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted activities/use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants support research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to the creation and publication of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should describe and justify how funds will be used for those activities in their proposal and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application instructions: follow the Notice of Funding Opportunity and Grants.gov rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity to ensure you understand all the expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this program and are prepared to write the most effective application. Follow the instructions outlined in the Notice of Funding Opportunity and Grants.gov instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must adhere closely to all instructions in the NOFO and Grants.gov package; changes in rules (e.g., writing sample format) are announced in the NOFO and program pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and submit via Grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Register for a Grants.gov account; submit your application package on Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register as soon as you know you are going to apply; ensure your registration is current. Grants.gov resources (individual registration instructions, knowledge base, applicant tools) and technical tips (download Adobe Reader, tips for making PDFs) are recommended to prevent submission issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing sample: length and format requirements (revised)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules about the length and format of the required writing sample have been revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the current Notice of Funding Opportunity and program resources for the exact, up-to-date requirements and examine sample application narratives to model their writing sample accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission confirmations and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit your application, Grants.gov will send you up to five e-mail messages confirming receipt of your application. You should verify that you have received all confirmation messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam/junk folders for Grants.gov messages. After the fifth Grants.gov message (confirming NEH received your application), use NEH’s secure area with your application number and Grants.gov tracking number to monitor the status of letters and the application. Applicants are responsible for ensuring required materials are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation: NEH requests and applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program staff will request letters of reference from your recommenders on or about January 9 (a little over one full month after the application deadline). You will be notified by e-mail when each of your letters of reference has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may check the names and e-mail addresses of letter writers and whether their letters have arrived via NEH’s secure area; if necessary, applicants may send reminders to letter writers (including the upload link). Applicants are responsible for ensuring that their letter writers have received the solicitations and submitted letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use program resources and examples to prepare a competitive application
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Resources include the Public Scholar FAQ, list of recently funded projects, sample application narratives, and a recorded online information session that explained goals, eligibility, review, and how to write an effective application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the recorded information session (presentation + Q&A), review sample application narratives (titles provided), and consult the FAQ and list of funded projects to understand scope, expectations, and presentation of successful proposals.
